questions.stem: A scientist adds a substance that prevents ATP from being formed in a cell culture. Which cellular process would be most immediately affected?

options.text: Storage of fat in adipose tissue
Active transport of ions across cell membranes
Diffusion of oxygen into the cells
Osmosis of water into the cells

questions.explanation: Active transport requires energy from ATP to move substances against their concentration gradient. Without ATP production, active transport would stop immediately. Diffusion and osmosis are passive processes that do not require ATP.

questions.stem: ATP is often described as the 'energy currency' of the cell. Which analogy best explains why?

options.text: Like money, ATP is stored in large amounts and used infrequently
Like a rechargeable battery, ATP can be broken down to release energy and reformed from ADP and phosphate
Like food, ATP is consumed once and cannot be recycled
Like oxygen, ATP is only obtained from the environment

questions.explanation: ATP works like a rechargeable battery — it is broken down into ADP and phosphate to release energy for cellular processes, then reformed (recharged) using energy from respiration. This cycle of forming and breaking down ATP occurs continuously.

questions.stem: A muscle cell uses approximately 10 million ATP molecules per second during contraction. Why do muscle cells contain many mitochondria?

options.text: Mitochondria store large reserves of ATP for later use
Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, which produces the large quantities of ATP needed
Mitochondria produce glucose for the muscle cells to use
Mitochondria remove lactic acid from muscle cells

questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the organelles where aerobic respiration takes place, producing ATP. Muscle cells have high energy demands during contraction, so they contain many mitochondria to produce sufficient ATP. ATP is not stored in bulk — it is continuously made and used.

questions.stem: When ATP is hydrolysed (broken down), it releases energy along with ADP and an inorganic phosphate group. A cell uses this energy for protein synthesis. What must happen for the cell to continue making proteins?

options.text: The cell must obtain new ATP from the bloodstream
ADP and phosphate must be recombined into ATP using energy from respiration
The cell must switch to using glucose directly for energy
Protein synthesis can continue without ATP once it has started

questions.explanation: Cells continuously recycle ATP. After ATP is broken down to ADP and phosphate, energy from respiration is used to recombine them back into ATP. This ATP/ADP cycle is essential for maintaining a constant supply of energy for processes like protein synthesis.

questions.stem: A patient with a mitochondrial disease produces less ATP than normal. Which symptom would you most expect this patient to experience?

options.text: Improved athletic performance
Chronic fatigue and muscle weakness
Excessive weight gain due to increased glucose storage
Increased ability to concentrate

questions.explanation: With reduced ATP production, cells cannot carry out energy-requiring processes efficiently. Muscles require large amounts of ATP for contraction, so the patient would experience muscle weakness and chronic fatigue — common symptoms of mitochondrial diseases.
